title: The Saints on Earth and Those Above
description: The Saints on Earth and Those Above in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 453, “The Communion of Saints”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The saints on earth and those a-bove But one com-mu-nion make; Joined to their Lord in bonds of love, All of His grace par-take.

lines: The saints on earth and those above
Joined to their Lord in bonds of love,
One family, we dwell in Him;
Though now divided by the stream,
One army of the living God,
Part of the host have crossed the flood
O God, be Thou our constant guide!
Then, when the word is given,
Bid Thou death's flood its waves divide,
And land us safe in heaven.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
